record.paper_title: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems
record.context_brief: FA-1f convergence to equilibrium from any nontrivial initial state
record.original_question: Consider the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on the lattice Z with infection density q in (0,1), where a site may update only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and let π be the Bernoulli product equilibrium measure with density q of infected vertices. Is it true that for every such q, every initial distribution ν that almost surely contains at least one infected vertex, and every local observable f depending on finitely many sites, the law of the process converges locally to equilibrium in the sense that lim_{t→∞} |E_ν(f(η(t))) − π(f)| = 0?

evidence.quote: A second basic question is to determine under which conditions on q and on the initial distribution ν, the law of the process at time t converges to the equilibrium measure π as t → ∞. Natural choices for ν are the Bernoulli product measure µq0 with q0 > 0, q0 ≠ q or the Dirac mass on the configuration with a single infection at the origin. For FA-1, it is natural to conjecture the following. Conjecture 1. For any q ∈ (0, 1) and any function f depending on the state of finitely many vertices lim t→∞ |Eν(f(η(t))) − π(f)| = 0, (1.1) provided that ν(∃ an infected vertex) = 1.

For the FA-1f process the constraint satisfies cx(η) = 1{ηx−1+ηx+1̸=2}. Informally, FA-1f can be described via its so-called graphical representation as follows: each vertex x ∈ Z is equipped with a unit intensity Poisson process... if the current configuration has at least one empty site among the nearest neighbours of x, we update the state of x

Let $\eta(t) = (\eta_x(t))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the one-dimensional Fredrickson–Andersen one-spin facilitated (FA-1f) process, defined as the continuous-time Markov process on $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ (where state $1$ at site $x$ means "infected/empty" and $0$ means "healthy/filled") with the following dynamics. Fix a parameter $q \in (0,1)$, and set $p = 1-q$. Each site $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ carries an independent rate-one Poisson clock; at the ring times of $x$, if at least one of the nearest neighbours $x-1, x+1$ is in state $1$ (i.e. the kinetic constraint $c_x(\eta) = \mathbf{1}_{\{\eta_{x-1}+\eta_{x+1} 
eq 0\}}$ is satisfied), then $\eta_x$ is refreshed to $1$ with probability $q$ and to $0$ with probability $p$, independently of everything else; if the constraint is not satisfied, no update occurs. The Bernoulli product measure $\pi$ on $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\pi(\eta_x = 1) = q$ for all $x$ is reversible for this dynamics.

artifact.status_search_result: Convergence to equilibrium for FA-1f on $\mathbb{Z}$ has been established when $q$ is sufficiently large (above an explicit threshold $\bar q < 1$), with exponential rate in dimension one, by Blondel, Cancrini, Martinelli, Roberto and Toninelli. The full conjecture, asserting local convergence for every $q\in(0,1)$ and every initial law that almost surely contains an infected site, remains open in the small-$q$ regime, where the non-stationary dynamics is poorly understood.

status_evidence.title: Fredrickson-Andersen one spin facilitated model out of equilibrium
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence to equilibrium has been proven when the vacancy density q is above a proper threshold q̄<1, with exponential rate on Z and stretched exponential for d>1.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence to equilibrium for FA-1f is known only for q above a threshold, leaving the small-q regime open.

status_evidence.title: Front evolution of the Fredrickson-Andersen one spin facilitated model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the front evolution for FA-1f, with non-equilibrium behaviour at general q remaining a subject of active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Non-stationary behaviour of FA-1f at general q is still under active study, indicating the conjecture is not fully resolved.
